'''2005 Corellia Regional Kevin Brownell DS Set Your Course For Alderaan''' was the Dark Side constructed list played by [[Kevin Brownell]] at [[2005 Corellia Regional]]; the list below is as posted on DeckTech by Kevin "Cubs Fan" Brownell (2005-01-23).<ref name="src">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/decks/decks.php?deck=34382 Still In The Navy, And Probably Will Be For Life]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050221140437/http://www.decktech.net:80/starwarsccg/decks/decks.php?deck=34382 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Original post ==

'''Still In The Navy, And Probably Will Be For Life'''
* '''Author:''' Kevin "Cubs Fan" Brownell
* '''Published:''' January 23, 2005
* '''Rating:''' 4.78
* '''Description:''' A powerful Big Blue weapons-based deck that can stand up to any light side space package. Went 3-0 at the Corellia Regional. Please read strategy section before reviewing, thanks.

=== Strategy ===

Strategy is fairly basic...do the first-turn Executor trick (use Mob. Pts. to pull Executor, use We're The Bait (v) to pull TMNALTC, use KDY (v) to pull Baspin).  Get an Admiral on it, which should be fairly easy with the number of Admirals and the two Commands.  Pull out your systems and cover them with destroyers.  Move the Death Star and get 2 FWKTIL (v) damage going.  Drain, using Chiraneau for an extra +1.

When it comes to fighting, this deck packs a punch.  Defensive Fire (v) usually means you'll be firing first, so kill off the light side's more powerful ships (e.g. virtual Bright Hope, Outrider, etc.) before they can hurt you.  Flawless Marksmanship helps, as does the +3 from the Laser Cannon Batteries themselves (except when using Defensive Fire).  With Intensify The Forward Batteries, you can pretty much hit any capital ship, even the Home One.  And the beauty of it is, hitting ships basically gets you around Savrip...they have to lose the ships from the table anyway.  Plus, each ship you hit costs your opponent one force.  You can hit 2 ships per turn (and up the damage with Artillery).

This deck also can deploy quickly b/c the destroyers deploy -1 with Ozzel, the unique ones -1 with KDY (v), Piett is another -1, Motti -2, and the virtual destroyers are -3.

Individual card choices:

Kuat Drive Yards (v) - yeah, I know it limits my FWKTIL damage, but I don't often do much more than 2-4 in a turn anyway, so I want to take advantage of the guarantee of getting my systems out without having to pull a billion cards to do it (like with the docking bay/Piett/Merrejk trick).

Precision Targeting (v) - this card is sweet, fire twice in a turn and always get the first shot in.  With Relentless Pursuit, this card is devastating.

Intensify The Forward Batteries - pullable with Piett, is a floating destiny 6, and reduces armor of cap. ships by 4.  No ship is safe.

D* Assault Squadron - this card is in here for one reason only...MBO.  It's tech against the worst matchup (-6 to Attack Run), without costing me more than one card slot.  It's also pullable with the objective.

Gravity Shadow - my all-time favorite card.  It's a major surprise to any light side deck that's running from you in space.  Trap a single ship, and unless there's a Houjix, game over.  It also has the side benefit of blowing stuff up.  At the Corellia Regional, I blew up one of my QMC opponent's better ships (can't remember which one).  I may take out the War Room to put another in.

Sidious - can sit at the D* Docking Bay for purposes of Battle Plan/Order and Resistance.  I take no battle damage there and he's immune to attrition, so he's basically impossible to take down (unless you can manage to hit him with a lightsaber).  Why not the destiny-6 Emperor?  B/c unlike him, Sidious can deploy to the DB with opponent's characters present.  I always hated it when my opponent dropped people there early and Emperor became useless.

War Room - pullable extra force generation.

Bottom line, this deck is easily adapted to any light side deck and works fairly quickly.  Against weaker space packages, I can set up fast and drain and do FWKTIL damage while my UC spies slow the opponent down.  Against space-heavy decks I just battle and shoot all his ships down.  This deck has worked extremely well and I will continue to use it at major events.  Thanks for your reviews.
